title: Reduce GPU queue amplification via proactive scaling, priority scheduling, and throttled rerouting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up for the Feb 27 GPU capacity event: root-cause analysis and targeted fixes to stop request queue amplification (long-tail enqueueing) in hosted API GPU pools. Scope includes admission controller fixes, priority-aware scheduling, autoscaler threshold tuning, and a short-term request rerouting policy to lower tail 95/99 latency and reduce 429s during bursts.
impact: During the incident hosted API experienced GPU pool saturation for 18 minutes across us-west-2, causing a sustained increase in tail latency (p95 +420ms, p99 spiked to 2.9s) and a 27% increase in 429/503 errors for model-large routes. Several paying customers reported degraded experiences and one customer escalated to Support with a P1.
root_cause_summary: Three factors combined to amplify queue growth: (1) an admission controller regression removed an early fast-fail path for long-prefill requests, allowing them to enqueue and hold KV cache resources; (2) autoscaler hysteresis and high cooldown windows prevented timely GPU scale-up during short bursts; (3) scheduling lacked request priority, so expensive background/low-priority requests could block foreground low-latency requests.
action_items: A1: Reintroduce and harden fast-fail admission checks for prefill/long-running requests (owner: Marco R., ETA: 2026-03-10, status: Done)
A2: Implement request priority tagging and priority-aware scheduling in the runtime (owner: Priya N., ETA: 2026-03-21, status: In Progress)
A3: Reduce autoscaler cooldown and add burst detection (owner: Tobias K., ETA: 2026-03-18, status: In Progress)
A4: Add short-circuit reroute policy to divert best-effort requests to lower-cost model variants when pool saturation detected (owner: Marco R., ETA: 2026-03-25, status: Planned)
A5: Add synthetic workload test to CI that reproduces queue amplification pattern and validates admission behavior (owner: QA Team, ETA: 2026-03-14, status: In Progress)
A6: Dashboard & alerting: add a composite alert for queue-growth velocity + GPU utilization to trigger on-call before 80% saturation (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-12, status: Done)
A7: Post-deploy validation runbook for canary + load replay to ensure no regression in admission or autoscaling behavior (owner: Marco R., ETA: 2026-03-20, status: In Progress)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial incident triage completed; confirmed admission regression introduced in runtime change set rtm-2.0.7.
2026-03-04: Fast-fail admission patch implemented and validated in staging with synthetic prefill workload — eliminated long-tail enqueueing in test harness.
2026-03-06: Autoscaler tuning experiment: lowered cooldown from 5m -> 90s in a dedicated test pool; observed 45% faster scale-up during 1-3 minute bursts.
2026-03-08: Design session for priority scheduling and tagging; agreed on three priority classes (interactive, background, best-effort) and LPQ (limited proportional queue) algorithm.
2026-03-10: SRE added composite queue-growth alert to PagerDuty; fired during controlled test and validated runbook execution.
2026-03-12: QA started CI synthetic test integration; initial failures found in a rare race condition when admission and eviction run concurrently — PR created to serialize those operations.
2026-03-14: Canary rollout of admission fast-fail patch to 10% of traffic in us-west-2; metrics show p99 latency reduced by 18% on canary subset.
2026-03-14: Next focus: finish priority scheduling implementation and implement reroute policy for best-effort traffic.
Review notes: PM requested a clear rollback plan for the autoscaler cooldown change; SRE provided a scoped revert playbook and automated flag toggle.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed admission fast-fail fixes to all hosted clusters with no increase in client-side error rate.
Priority-aware scheduling in runtime reduces p99 latency on interactive routes by >= 15% under replayed burst workloads.
Autoscaler changes trigger scale-up within 120s for sustained burst patterns and do not cause oscillation in 95% of test runs.
Synthetic CI test reproduces queue amplification and fails when admission or priority scheduling regress; test added to gating suite.
Runbook and dashboards updated; composite alert validated in staging and on-call runbook exercised at least once.
next_steps: Finish and land priority scheduler prototype (Priya N.) and start canary on 5% traffic next week.
Implement reroute policy to fallback best-effort requests to model-small variants as short-term mitigation (Marco R.).
Complete CI synthetic test and add to gating; run full replay against canary clusters before 100% rollout.
Coordinate with Support to communicate mitigation timeline to affected customers and include link to public incident summary.
Post-deploy: run a focused chaos test that simulates GPU drop and validate autoscaler + admission interactions.
notes: This ticket bundles technical debt (admission race fixes) with feature work (priority scheduling). Keep changes small and reversible; avoid coupling autoscaler logic to scheduler until priority behavior is stable. Triage follow-ups into separate ENG tickets once design is finalized.
